question.text: An investor with a gold ETF priced in INR sees gold appreciating 15% in USD terms but the ETF rises only 10% due to INR appreciation against USD. How can the investor reduce the embedded USDINR currency component?

answer.text: Short USDINR currency futures (or buy USDINR put options) for the investment amount and matching tenor to reduce the USDINR risk embedded in the gold ETF return
Buy USDINR currency futures to amplify returns from both gold and currency appreciation
Switch from a gold ETF to physical gold to avoid currency risk entirely
Buy EURINR futures to hedge against the rupee appreciation

explanation.text: The Logic: A gold ETF in INR is affected by both gold in USD and the USDINR exchange rate. If INR appreciates 5% against USD, the ETF gain is reduced by roughly that amount (here 15% − 5% ≈ 10%). Shorting USDINR futures, or buying USDINR puts, for the investment notional and matching tenor offsets the USDINR component — losses from INR appreciation on the ETF are compensated by gains on the short futures / long put. The Trap: Buying USDINR futures would add MORE currency exposure rather than reduce it. Physical gold priced in INR carries the same USDINR exposure. EURINR is a different currency pair and does not hedge the USDINR component. Note: The Currency Derivatives workbook explicitly cautions that currency futures may not completely remove spot USDINR risk because futures pricing also depends on changes in the futures premium/discount over the holding period — so this is a reduction/hedge of USDINR risk, not a perfect elimination.
